name: Ignite
label: Revelation
lede: An Orange County hardcore band with a Hungarian heart, a U2 cover its label wouldn't allow, and a singer who spent two years fronting Pennywise before coming home.

eras.title: Fuse, Angerslave, Shade, then Ignite
eras.text: Bassist Brett Rasmussen and guitarist Joe D. Foster went through three band names before landing on Ignite. The debut had two different singers on it, and the man who would define the band, Zoli Téglás, only arrived once it was done.

years.h: Brett Rasmussen and Joe D. Foster settle on the name Ignite
years.p: After trying out Fuse, Angerslave and Shade, Brett Rasmussen and Joe D. Foster's Orange County band becomes Ignite, with Joe Nelson and [[Gavin Oglesby|55402ba0-2241-4a42-9270-386964a84a79]] joining and [[Casey Jones|2a3fce86-361f-4deb-aefa-c711654de661]] on drums.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rasmussen and Foster first started playing together in 1992. Ignite's first demo carried five songs: Ash Return, Distance, Slow, Should Have Known and Far Away.

years.h: Scarred for Life, Ignite's debut · Lost & Found
years.p: Cut at Moonsong Studios in Riverside, California. Randy Johnson sings tracks 1 to 5 and Joe Nelson sings 6 to 8, over Brett Rasmussen, Joe D. Foster and Casey Jones.

years.h: Zoli Téglás becomes Ignite's permanent singer
years.p: With Scarred for Life finished, Ignite recruit Zoltán "Zoli" Téglás, the California-born son of Hungarian immigrants. He stays 27 years.
years.xp:
Téglás was born on November 10, 1969. His father came to the US after World War II and his mother in the 1960s, and he grew up speaking Hungarian and spending childhood summers in Veresegyház, outside Budapest.

His own Wikipedia entry dates his arrival in Ignite to 1993; the band's entry says he came in after Scarred for Life was recorded.

eras.title: Big in Berlin, signed to Revelation
eras.text: Label trouble at home sent Ignite to Europe: a Berlin label put out their records, and German crowds made them one of the best live bands on the continent. Revelation Records got them in America for an EP and a split, and then the original line-up broke apart.

years.h: Family: Zoli Téglás's first Ignite album
years.p: Ten songs in 26 minutes, made at For the Record St. in Orange County with producer Jim Monroe and released in Europe by Lost & Found.
years.xp: The same year brought the In My Time EP. With a label dispute in the way, Ignite went to Berlin's Conversion Records, which issued Call on My Brothers in America, built from the European material.

years.h: Ignite and [[Good Riddance|ab4725b8-7a2f-429a-a55a-3dde07c9acea]] split a 7" · Revelation REV 53
years.p: Ignite's first Revelation release. According to Revelation's own pressing notes, some of the 2,000 black vinyl first pressing came out with the two bands' labels switched.

years.h: Past Our Means EP · Revelation REV 54
years.p: Six songs in 14 minutes, recorded April 22–26 at Paramount Studios. The closer, Taken Away, is Zoli Téglás writing about Hungary.
years.xp: Produced by Jim Goodwin and the band. Revelation pressed 2,840 on black and 323 on blue the first time around, and has kept it in print since, most recently remastered in 2016.

years.h: Ignite tour Japan and Europe with [[Millencolin|a11aacf5-fcbe-47f9-b065-75f4466c00ae]] and [[Madball|c9e0a0f5-9f53-4247-a52d-a3f29d975e17]]
years.p: On the back of those tours, German magazine VISIONS names Ignite the third best live band of 1996.

years.h: Casey Jones and Joe D. Foster leave Ignite
years.p: Drummer Casey Jones quits without warning. Scott Golley fills in before [[Craig Anderson|08c50d56-7783-4411-bd94-36ffd87e11e7]] takes the drum stool for good, and Brian Balchack replaces co-founder Joe D. Foster on guitar.

eras.title: The cover TVT wouldn't allow
eras.text: Ignite's breakthrough came on a New York label, TVT, with A Place Called Home. Zoli Téglás sang about veterans and poverty in English and Hungarian, and did stunt work on the side until a film injury hurt his spine. The U2 cover TVT refused finally came out six years later.

years.h: Zoli Téglás injures his spine on a Jackie Chan film
years.p: Between tours, Ignite's singer works as a stunt performer. According to Wikipedia, he suffered a serious spinal injury on a Jackie Chan production.

years.h: A Place Called Home · TVT Records
years.p: Ignite's breakthrough: 13 tracks including Veteran and Who Sold Out Now, plus a version of the title track sung in Hungarian.
years.xp:
Producer Cameron Webb started working with the band in 1999 pre-production and stayed with them for the next two decades; the album itself credits Thom Wilson and Zoli Téglás as producers. Punknews called Ignite one of the most unique hardcore acts it had heard in years.

Europe got the album in February 2001, timed to Ignite's run on the Vans Club Tour.

years.h: Revelation presses Call on My Brothers on vinyl · REV 91
years.p: Revelation gives Ignite's 1995 Conversion album its own 12", starting with 538 copies on opaque purple, and keeps re-pressing it through 2016.

years.h: Zoli Téglás sings with the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]]
years.p: Ignite's singer joins the Misfits for North American tour dates in 2000, and starts his side project, Zoli Band, the same year.

years.h: Nik Hill joins as Ignite play the Persistence Tour
years.p: Ignite play the European Persistence Tour package. Guitarist [[Nik Hill|8a49a504-827e-45ae-aec9-a3837e106b55]] joins, and later starts Nations Afire with Brett Rasmussen and [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]]'s Chris Chasse.

years.h: Ignite's Troubadour DVD is shot, then shelved
years.p: Ignite film a live DVD at The Troubadour in West Hollywood with A Dying Dream and Eightyonedays. Technical problems keep it from ever coming out.

years.h: Ignite sign to Abacus, Century Media's punk imprint
years.p: The deal that brings Ignite back to making albums after five years.

years.big: TVT said no. Sunday Bloody Sunday, six years late.
years.h: Our Darkest Days finally carries Ignite's U2 cover
years.p: TVT had vetoed Ignite's cover of U2's Sunday Bloody Sunday for A Place Called Home. It closes out Our Darkest Days on Abacus instead, produced by Cameron Webb.
years.xp:
The album takes aim at the Iraq war and the Bush administration, with songs like Poverty for All and Know Your History. A hidden track in Hungarian sits at the end of the last song.

The Bleeding video, directed by Christopher Sims, came out on July 12, 2006. Nik Hill left that year to start Lucky Scars.

eras.title: On loan to Pennywise
eras.text: Ignite headlined the Persistence Tour, then lost their singer to a bigger band. For almost three years Zoli Téglás fronted Pennywise, until his back gave out on a German stage, and Ignite went quiet.

years.h: Ignite headline the Persistence Tour
years.p: Six years after playing the European hardcore package, Ignite top the bill.

years.h: Zoli Téglás replaces Jim Lindberg in [[Pennywise|5c210861-2ce2-4be3-9307-bbcfc361cc01]]
years.p: Ignite's singer takes over from Jim Lindberg in Pennywise. Ignite stay together and tour when they can, while Téglás juggles Pennywise, Ignite and a solo album.

years.h: Zoli Téglás collapses on stage at With Full Force
years.p: A herniated disc drops Pennywise's singer to his knees mid-set at Germany's With Full Force festival. Loudwire reported doctors warned of possible paralysis; he had emergency back surgery on June 30.
years.xp: Pennywise cancelled the rest of that European leg. Téglás's only Pennywise album, All or Nothing, came out in 2012, and he left the band that October; Jim Lindberg later returned.

years.h: Ignite go on full hiatus
years.p: After three years of sporadic tours around Zoli Téglás's Pennywise schedule, Ignite stop entirely.

eras.title: A chart debut at 22
eras.text: Ignite came back with Zoli Téglás and made their first album in a decade. It charted in Germany and Hungary, and Téglás moved into his grandmother's house outside Budapest before walking away from the band in 2019.

years.h: Ignite return and start their fifth album
years.p: Zoli Téglás is back full time, and Ignite begin recording with Cameron Webb again.

years.h: A War Against You hits No. 12 in Germany
years.p: Ignite's first chart entry anywhere, 22 years into the band: No. 12 in Germany and No. 5 in Hungary, on Century Media.

years.h: Two nights at Budapest's Barba Negra, and a new tattoo
years.p: Playing Budapest, Zoli Téglás gets the Hungarian flag with the 1956 hole cut in it tattooed on his arm, with the words Never forget.
years.xp:
He told Daily News Hungary the idea came after a visit to Budapest's House of Terror museum, when a taxi driver asked him why he dwelled on the past. By then he'd inherited his grandmother's house in Veresegyház and moved in.

He also said hardcore barely exists in the USA anymore, with not many people to play for.

q: With a heavy heart I am announcing my departure from Ignite.
years.h: Zoli Téglás leaves Ignite after 27 years
years.p: Ignite's singer says he will spend his time rescuing animals and on film and music projects. He plays the California dates already booked for early 2020, then he's gone.
years.xp: Téglás founded the Pelican Rescue Team, which picks up injured seabirds on the California coast and drives them to rehab centers, and volunteers as music and outreach coordinator for the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society. He also turns up in Terminator: Dark Fate (2019).

eras.title: Any metal guys who can hit the notes?
eras.text: Ignite didn't fold. Brett Rasmussen asked around for a singer with range, Holy Grail guitarist Eli Santana talked his way into an audition, and the band made its first album in six years.

q: I happened to be well into my cups.
years.h: Eli Santana announced as Ignite's new singer
years.p: Brett Rasmussen asked drummer Craig Anderson if he knew any metal guys who could hit the notes. Anderson called Holy Grail guitarist Eli Santana, who asked to try out.
years.xp: Santana auditioned by singing two existing Ignite songs, then new material. The band introduced him with the Anti-Complicity Anthem EP and video, which also carried Turn XXI.

years.cap: Punk in the Park, Silverado, California
years.h: Eli Santana's first Ignite show: Punk in the Park, Silverado
years.p: Santana debuts in front of thousands at Punk in the Park in Silverado, California, on a bill with [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]] and [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]].

years.h: Ignite, the self-titled album with Eli Santana
years.p: Nine new songs on Century Media, produced by Cameron Webb, Ignite's first album in six years.

yt: Sunday Bloody Sunday live, Hamden CT, September 2024
years.h: Thirty years of Ignite, on the road with [[Slapshot|efc798e2-3165-49fd-a83b-d659cdb20488]]
years.p: Ignite tour the East Coast with Slapshot, Death by Stereo and School Drugs, then mark 30 years with a European run, again with Slapshot.

years.h: Zoli Téglás on CBS Evening News, rescuing pelicans
years.p: Ignite's former singer appears on CBS Evening News to talk about his Pelican Rescue Team and its work on the California coast.
